text:
maria: quick question about the embeddings endpoint behavior — trying to finalize SDK and docs for next release. specifically: how do we handle mixed input arrays with nulls / empty strings, truncation semantics, and batch limits? need a short canonical answer we can put in the spec.

kai: short, informal: we preserve ordering and return one entry per input. currently we return `null` for `null` inputs and a full-dimension vector for `""` (empty string). truncation happens on token count (model-side). max_batch_items today is 1024 in prod but the runtime can be tuned.

jonathan: adding context — this has bitten a few clients: some SDKs drop `null`s when serializing JSON arrays which shifts indexes. spec should say "do not drop items; responses are 1:1 with request inputs". also we want output vectors to always be the model's dim when not null.

irina: model/embedding note: embedding model produces fixed-length float arrays (e.g. 1536). we don't produce variable-length embeddings. truncation is token-based, using our sentencepiece tokenizer; when truncated we currently set a response header `x-redwood-embed-truncated: true` (plan).

maria: example payload to be explicit (for SDK folks):
```json
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "rwd-embed-1",
  "input": ["hello world", "", null, "long text..."]
}
```
expected response (proto): array with same length, e.g. `[ [0.12, ...], [0.0, ...], null, [0.34, ...] ]` — i.e. `null` preserved in place.

kai: question: do we want `null` or an array of zeros for missing inputs? pros: `null` is explicit and easy to detect. zeros might be ambiguous (could be a real vector). i'd vote for `null` and a clear SDK contract.

jonathan: agree with `null`. also add `preserve_input_length=true` language to the contract; no client should rely on items being removed. backward-compat: older clients sometimes expected missing entries to be omitted — we should call that out.

irina: truncation detail: we truncate by token so embeddings for very long strings are from truncated text. for transparency, include `x-redwood-embed-truncated` and `x-redwood-embed-trunc-tokens` headers when truncation occurs. that helps quality monitoring.

maria: batch limits — 1024 is current safe default, but we have some internal configs allowing 2048 for certain Dedicated pools. propose we document `max_batch_items: 1024` in public API and add `x-redwood-batch-truncated` header when server enforces batch size reduction.

kai: SDK action: i'll open a JS SDK PR to ensure: 1) `null`s are preserved (don't filter out), 2) we surface `x-redwood-embed-truncated` on the response, and 3) we add a warning when input items > 1024 (client-side check). i'll tag reviewers.

jonathan: ops/compat action: i'll update the API spec doc + changelog note about `null` behavior and headers. should we add an opt-in `coerce_nulls` query param for older clients? lean no — prefer server stable contract.

maria: ok. can someone volunteer to add unit tests on runtime side to assert: null preserved, empty string returns vector, ordering preserved, header set when truncation occurs?

irina: i'll add the model-level unit tests; kai can add SDK tests; jonathan can add runtime integration tests.

kai: picking up SDK tests + PR today. tagging @jonathan for spec review when you're ready. :thumbsup:

jonathan: will update spec doc by EOD and add changelog entry.

deploy-bot: scheduled deploy to staging at 2026-03-18T02:00Z for spec + runtime test changes.

maria: perfect. i'll consolidate notes and open a single tracking issue linking the three PRs. thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
